top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, prose-based citation) is my first choice on the common criteria. His voice is distinctive. His formal ambition is structural: memory, the body, dream and the city are built into large architectures rather than treated as separate themes. The linguistic density appears to be part of the achievement and not decoration. Public critical accounts describe Solenoid as a restructuring of the earlier Orbitor project and not a repetition, which supports sustained depth across the oeuvre. I rely on translation and public critical knowledge, not verified close reading of the Romanian. I cannot settle whether the late long books deepen the project or become excessive, and I cannot assess his poetry, so I would keep it out of the citation. P002 (Anne Carson, with the narrow citation on lyric, verse narrative and essay) is a close second. That narrowing resolves most of my earlier concern about translations and scholarship. What remains open is whether her later books sustain the depth of Autobiography of Red and Nox, and whether her classically allusive English travels across languages. Both candidates are far preferable to P000, because the shortlist contains serious, well-argued literary cases. I give no weight to the number of colleagues backing either candidate, to fame, or to my own simulated vote.
